feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles: the scope, progression, and public-sector specialization come through clearly. It is well written overall, but impact would improve with tighter structure, less repetition across skills sections, and more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership credibility in digital platforms, governance, and communications.  
- Good evidence of scale and complexity: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms make the experience believable and concrete.  
- Writing is polished and professional, with no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors; tone is consistent and appropriately executive.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve scannability and free space for achievements.  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities (“led,” “built,” “advised”) without showing business outcomes such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, or cost/time savings.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; date style varies slightly (“Oct.”/“Sept.”), and “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “French (A2, learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic “building the platforms” language with sharper action verbs and outcomes, e.g. “leading modernization” or “scaling.”
- Add 1–2 proof points from recent roles to increase impact, such as “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related capabilities and reducing list-like phrasing.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Built and scaled enterprise digital systems supporting a 10,000+ page Drupal platform, 3.5M annual page views, and 50+ internal publishers, spanning analytics, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; consider using the intro for proof points instead of another positioning statement.
- The capability list closely mirrors Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into sharper, less repetitive capability areas with more consistent phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and trim filler terms like “operations” where possible.
- Emphasize the most distinctive, recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search, and automation.
- Consider this tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming
- Standardize style: replace “website” with “web” for brevity and use “and” instead of “&” if the rest of the CV follows a more formal tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” closely overlaps with Header and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” repeats content already covered in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent NACo roles. Tightening the phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinctive and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Emphasize outcomes where possible: e.g., “to improve policy-content discovery,” “to support ongoing campaign expansion,” “to extend conference engagement.”
- Standardize style and specificity: use consistent verbs (“Led,” “Built,” “Developed”), hyphenation (“bill-level”), and number style (“10 x 20-foot” or “10-by-20-foot”).
- Consider this tighter wording: “Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a modular architecture for future campaign growth.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current consultant and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider foregrounding it or adding projects not already described elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles by emphasizing advisory scope, platform delivery, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, campaign platforms, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 outcome-oriented points; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet.
- Replace generic phrasing with stronger verbs and scope: “Designed Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkit experiences” and “Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of microsites/toolkits launched, workflow improvements, search accuracy, engagement lift, reduced publishing time, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and coordinated communications” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this item focused on consultant-level advisory and build work.
- The AI search and microsite work also appears in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same detail verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the most distinctive wins first: Drupal migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.
- Add outcome language where possible: site performance, publishing efficiency, reporting speed, campaign capacity, cost savings, or reduced vendor reliance.
- Condense channel oversight bullet: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders” rather than listing every platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this higher-level and strategic.
- Video/programming language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building enterprise capacity (studio, systems, scale).

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to the transition from execution to systems leadership, and tighten phrasing around outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague lines with systems language: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helped improve consistency and effectiveness” is too soft and repeats governance/workflow themes already covered in the Director role.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with sharper, differentiated language tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content governance and planning” or “Structured content strategy” to better reflect the Drupal/governance work.
- Keep wording parallel: noun phrases only, no mixed styles.
- If space allows, prioritize “content operations” and “governance” over “messaging,” since messaging is already evident in work history.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; use this section to add nuance, not repeat.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization outcomes rather than listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here if they are not central to recent work: consider removing jQuery and possibly WordPress/SharePoint unless they are important targets for the role.
- Use broader phrasing like “enterprise CMS platforms” or “platform integration” to sound more senior and align with recent NACo work.
- If space allows, tie to scale indirectly: “enterprise web platforms” or “high-volume public-facing sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current list duplicates the detailed “Technical + IT” section almost line-for-line.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats Core Competencies and recent project content.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets if space is tight.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business-facing wording: “KPI framework development,” “executive reporting,” “SEO and digital performance analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive dashboarding/reporting.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more specialized and operational so it adds detail rather than repeating “multimedia production.”

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a tighter, more distinctive skills cluster: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event production • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event technical direction • Post-production editing”
- Replace broad phrases like “studio operations” with higher-value wording such as “studio systems” or “technical direction.”
- If accurate, add scope/tool specificity to strengthen credibility: e.g., “multi-camera livestream workflows,” “broadcast-quality in-house studio production,” or “virtual/hybrid event delivery.”
- Keep this section skills-focused; save outcomes like studio buildout or recurring advocacy programming for recent NACo experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Video production and editing” duplicates “multimedia production” already stated in the header, core competencies, and work history.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “livestream operations” in Core Competencies; use more specific wording here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either add context on level of use or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, custom content structures) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put the strongest, most recent platform first and add brief qualifiers only where they reinforce recent impact.
- If space allows, make it outcome-linked: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 50+ publishers)**, since Drupal is clearly the most relevant platform in recent roles.
- Keep weaker/older tools unqualified unless you have meaningful scale or ownership to show.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or using this section for only platform names and the other for broader capabilities.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus your enterprise profile unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers (**HTML5, CSS3**) unless required by the role; they add little value at this level.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work, e.g. **Used for Drupal microsites, analytics deployment, workflow automation and lightweight edge/serverless solutions**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already appear under **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the same phrasing in both places.
- Consider removing **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent projects; it can make the stack feel dated.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and mixes automation platforms with project/collaboration tools. It also repeats “workflow automation” already stated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, so it should be tighter and more clearly categorized.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to improve scanability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Work Management & Collaboration Tools” so the title matches the content.
- Put the strongest/most relevant tools first based on recent work: Airtable, Power Automate, Jira/Asana likely matter more than Basecamp/Trello.
- If accurate, replace generic listing with light specificity: “Airtable workflow systems, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are generic workplace tools; keep only if they support a systems/operations positioning.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and misses the scale/ownership already shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations and member engagement rather than just naming platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign deployment)**
- If accurate, add one qualifier tied to recent work: **Used to support newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders**
- Keep only the strongest/current systems; if Mailchimp was limited or older, move it last or remove it to emphasize more enterprise-grade platforms

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This already overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters; avoid repeating audience scale here unless you remove it from a weaker older role
- “Multi-channel communications operations” and email leadership are already covered elsewhere, so this line should stay tool-focused, not responsibility-focused

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to signal seniority through outcomes. Tighten it into a sharper technical stack and emphasize optimization methods rather than generic nouns.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Tag Manager • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Swap **Dashboarding** for a tool or capability with clearer value, e.g. **KPI reporting** or **conversion analysis**.
- If space allows, group by function for readability: **Analytics:** GA4, BigQuery, Clarity | **Reporting:** Power BI, Looker Studio | **Optimization:** SEO analysis, A/B testing.
- Only keep platforms you’ve clearly used in recent roles; this section should reinforce the NACo analytics infrastructure work, not broaden beyond evidence.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one or making this version more tool-specific.
- **SEO** and **A/B testing** are useful, but if not supported elsewhere with examples/results, they may read as lighter claims than the analytics platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with clearer scope and any available outputs or audience metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and video operations.”
- Add concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and recurring video updates; improved publishing workflows across channels.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised one digital media associate,” if accurate.
- If possible, add volume metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing cadence, event size, or audience reach.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or piloting the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this at a lighter, foundational level.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and any concrete project outputs, while keeping the rest concise.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a specific deliverable if possible (e.g., videos, reports, campaign assets, stakeholder briefings).
- If available, add scope or results: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.
- Consider a two-part structure: research/program support first, then digital/media contribution second.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing multimedia production here, since video/content leadership is covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- “Supporting organizational programs and policy work” is vague and may repeat later advocacy/editorial coordination language.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mixed capabilities bucket than a tools line. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to software/tools only, and move workflow-type items elsewhere if possible.
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator**
- If you want to retain production capability, make it outcome-oriented and more senior: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream production • Podcast production**
- Consider naming the section **Creative Tools & Production** if keeping both software and production capabilities in one line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **Livestream studio workflows** duplicates “livestream operations,” “studio operations,” and event production already emphasized elsewhere.
- **Podcast production** is supported by older experience only; keep it only if still relevant to target roles.
